P7699.corridor_notes: The Jilin Province Energy Development 14th Five-Year Plan (吉林省能源发展"十四五"规划, page ~24-25, verified via pdftotext of the archived PDF) lists '榆树－舒兰' (Yushu-Shulan) by name as one of six priority natural-gas pipeline projects under construction/planning during 2021-2025: '推进吉林－延吉、延吉－珲春、梅河口－桦甸、白山－靖宇－临江、松原－白城、榆树－舒兰等天然气管线项目建设。新建省内支干线管道1753公里，包括1条干线和15条支线' (advance construction of the Jilin-Yanji, Yanji-Hunchun, Meihekou-Huadian, Baishan-Jingyu-Linjiang, Songyuan-Baicheng, Yushu-Shulan gas pipeline projects; province-wide 1,753km of new trunk/branch pipeline, comprising 1 trunk line + 15 branches). Confirms it is one of the ~15 planned branch lines off the province's main gas backbone, but the source gives no station-level detail, alignment, or length specific to this segment. A separate 2026-01 Shulan municipal news item ('舒兰天然气管网正式通气运行' / 'total-investment-100M-yuan gas project') describes a LOCAL 54.6km medium-pressure CNG distribution network built inside Shulan's urban core, fed by trucked/CNG supply rather than a trunk pipeline from Yushu -- consistent with the Yushu-Shulan long-distance connector itself still being unbuilt (matches GEM's Status=proposed).
P7699.researcher_notes: No station-level (分输站/门站) name could be found for either endpoint despite multiple query variations ('榆树-舒兰输气管道', '舒兰 天然气管道 通气 环评', '舒兰市 天然气管道 榆树'). GEM's ResearcherNotes (already in the payload) says the original Wiki data link is invalid and no other info was found -- this pass corroborates the project's existence via an independent primary source (the province's own 14th FYP energy plan PDF, archived because the live xxgk.jl.gov.cn URL fails TLS verification through this environment -- a cert-chain issue, confirmed reachable via plain curl with 200 and via the Wayback snapshot) but could not go past county-city-level resolution for the route itself. Endpoints geocoded as Yushu and Shulan city centers/government-seat points -- the finest level sourced is the county-city name pairing itself, not a station or township.
